g.text: layer pattern, bars every ≈ 600 along the path

svg.text: Detail D1: eave, roof to wall
at the mid-span buttress, section A-A, 1:10 · piece plan 1:5
Roof outer layer 80, printed with the rest of the
piece; cladding on the outside face (dashed line).
Zig-zag bead 80 in a 160 zone; it touches the outer
layer and layer 2 every ≈ 600; the cells between are
open air pockets for ventilation.
Layer 2, 80: printed bead that curves to leave a
pocket for the bar.
Inner layer 1, 80, room side. Layers 1 and 2
together are the structural leaf: 160 at the base,
80 at the crown (layer 2 ends).
Rebar pocket Ø55 in the leaf, bar Ø12 every ≈ 600
along the path, grouted after placing.
Starter bars Ø12 from the ring beam into the
pockets, lap 650; roof bars stop where the load
allows (open).
Ring bars Ø12 in the pocket zone every 300
(assumed).
Ring beam 400 x 500, cast in place: 6 Ø16, stirrups
Ø8 / 150; embedded in the buttress notch.
Buttress 400 wide, 700 from the inner face (300
beyond the wall), L-shaped around the ring beam; top
flush with the roof base at +2.50.
Wall 400 printed, same pattern as the roof; Ø16 bars
in the pockets run from the footing into the beam
and on into the roof pockets (assumed).
from your sketches
assumed by me, to confirm
Notes
Layer pattern from your drawing: from the inside, 80 + 80
printed layers (the second curves round the bar), then a
160 zig-zag zone, then the 80 outer layer; 400 in total.
Roof thicknesses are square to the slope; the wall is
vertical. Black heavy lines and dots = rebar, white
lattice cells = open air, single hatch = printed concrete,
crossed hatch = ring beam cut in the section plane.
